theme: Thinking through a problem with evidence instead of blame, and looking out for neighbors who need extra help
premise: The Grid Goes Dark. When the town of Harlow Crossing loses power all at once during a heat wave, thirteen-year-old Nico Varga and his friend Essie Kwan have only a few hours before the hospital's backup batteries run out. Everyone blames a hacker, but the real cause is hiding in the grid's own wiring, and Nico has to find it before dark.

characters: Nico Varga, thirteen, fixes small appliances in his family's repair shop
Essie Kwan, Nico's best friend, who keeps a notebook of every clue
Reva Varga, Nico's older sister, who works at the town grid control room
Mr. Okafor, the town engineer trying to find the fault in time
facts: Harlow Crossing is an invented town whose power, water and streetlights run through one shared system called the Lumen Grid
The hospital's backup batteries will fail in about nine hours unless the main grid comes back on
Many neighbors suspect a hacker, but no evidence of an outside attack has turned up yet
avoid: violence, gore or anyone being badly hurt
real brands, companies, places or real people
any real religion, god or sacred rite
no patient is harmed on the page and no real power grid, city or hacking group is named; the danger is solved by careful checking, not a chase or a fight
